questions.prompt: The brave general tamed the wild horses before the battle.
questions.answer: Dux fortis equōs ferōs ante proelium domuit.

questions.prompt: Jupiter thundered from the dark sky, and the whole camp trembled.
questions.answer: Juppiter ex caelō obscūrō tonuit, et tōta castra tremuērunt.

questions.prompt: The old man forbade the boys to swim in the deep river.
questions.answer: Senex puerōs vetuit in flūmine altō natāre.

questions.prompt: The gladiators fought fiercely in the arena for many hours.
questions.answer: Gladiātōrēs multās hōrās in arēnā ācriter dīmicāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The surgeon cut the deep wound with a sharp knife.
questions.answer: Medicus vulnus altum cultrō acūtō secuit.

questions.prompt: The gods helped the weary sailors, tossed about by the storm.
questions.answer: Deī nautās fessōs, tempestāte iactātōs, jūvērunt.

questions.prompt: The trumpet sounded, and the standing soldiers advanced.
questions.answer: Tuba sonuit, et mīlitēs stantēs prōcessērunt.

questions.prompt: The girl unfolded the letter which her father had sent.
questions.answer: Puella epistulam quam pater mīserat explicāvit.

questions.prompt: The dry leaves rattled, driven by the winter wind.
questions.answer: Folia ārida, ventō hībernō ācta, crepuērunt.

questions.prompt: For three days the sick king had lain in his chamber.
questions.answer: Trēs diēs rēx aeger in cubiculō cubuerat.

questions.prompt: The waves sounded against the rocks all night long.
questions.answer: Undae tōtā nocte in saxa sonuērunt.

questions.prompt: Hercules tamed the fierce lion with his bare hands.
questions.answer: Herculēs leōnem ferōcem nūdīs manibus domuit.

questions.prompt: The maidservant washed the linen garments in the cold spring.
questions.answer: Ancilla vestēs līneās in fonte frīgidō lāvit.

questions.prompt: The consul forbade the citizens to leave the city at night.
questions.answer: Cōnsul cīvēs urbem nocte relinquere vetuit.

questions.prompt: The general unfolded his plan to the assembled centurions.
questions.answer: Imperātor cōnsilium suum centuriōnibus congregātīs explicāvit.

questions.prompt: The victors stood before the temple and gave thanks to the gods.
questions.answer: Victōrēs ante templum stetērunt et deīs grātiās ēgērunt.

questions.prompt: It thundered, and the frightened children lay hidden in the house.
questions.answer: Tonuit, et līberī territī in domō latuērunt.

questions.prompt: The armies fought before the walls of the besieged town.
questions.answer: Exercitūs prō moenibus oppidī obsessī dīmicāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The blacksmith rubbed the sword until it glittered.
questions.answer: Faber gladium fricuit dōnec micuit.

questions.prompt: The drunken guests drank much wine at the long feast.
questions.answer: Convīvae ēbriī multum vīnum in longā cēnā pōtāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The stars glittered in the silent night, while the shepherd lay beneath a tree.
questions.answer: Stēllae in nocte silentī micuērunt, dum pāstor sub arbore cubābat.

questions.prompt: With his fear tamed, the young man stood before the angry king.
questions.answer: Metū domitō, iuvenis ante rēgem īrātum stetit.

questions.prompt: The physician cut away the diseased flesh, and then washed his hands.
questions.answer: Medicus carnem morbidam secuit, deinde manūs lāvit.

questions.prompt: The gods have often helped us; therefore we drank wine at the altars.
questions.answer: Dī nōs saepe iūvērunt, itaque vīnum ad ārās pōtāvimus.

questions.prompt: When it had thundered, the frightened flocks stood trembling in the field.
questions.answer: Cum tonuisset, gregēs territī in agrō trementēs stetērunt.

questions.prompt: The old soldier, who fought in many wars, now lies quietly at home.
questions.answer: Veterānus mīles, quī in multīs bellīs dīmicāvit, nunc domī quiētē cubat.

questions.prompt: The maidservant rubbed the bronze mirror until it glittered brightly.
questions.answer: Ancilla speculum aēneum fricuit dōnec clārē micāret.

questions.prompt: The magistrate forbade the merchants to sail, because the sea sounded threatening.
questions.answer: Magistrātus mercātōrēs nāvigāre vetuit, quod mare mināx sonābat.

questions.prompt: The poet unfolded the ancient scroll and recited the old verses in a clear voice.
questions.answer: Poēta volūmen antīquum explicāvit et versūs veterēs clārā vōce recitāvit.

questions.prompt: The ivy entwined the ancient wall, which had stood for many years.
questions.answer: Hedera mūrum vetustum implicuit, quī multōs annōs steterat.

questions.prompt: The weary travelers washed their feet and lay down beside the fire.
questions.answer: Fessī viātōrēs pedēs lāvērunt et prope ignem cubuērunt.

questions.prompt: The dry branches crackled in the flames, while the wind thundered outside.
questions.answer: Āridī rāmī in flammīs crepuērunt, dum ventus forīs tonābat.
